title: Artificial Intelligence: Understanding and Using AI Wisely
scope_note: Course scope: general education for adults and high-school students, not legal, medical or financial advice. No AI tool, account, download or paid service is needed: every example is prepared in advance and shown as text, and nothing runs. Examples labeled "fictional" were written for this course and are not real outputs of any named product. Laws, products and prices change; dated lessons say what to check. People and organizations in scenarios are fictional unless a lesson names a real case.

AI.AGENT.01.title: Tell a chatbot, a fixed tool-using workflow and an agent that chooses its own steps

AI.AGENT.02.title: Describe an agent's goal, tools, plan, feedback and stopping condition

AI.AGENT.03.title: Tell fixed scheduled automation from steps where a model makes choices, and where each is safer

AI.AGENT.04.title: Give an automated workflow only the access its task needs

AI.AGENT.05.title: Require a person to approve messages, payments, deletions and publication before they happen

AI.AGENT.06.title: Use logs to check what an automation did and prevent duplicate actions after retries

AI.BASICS.01.title: Describe AI in plain language as computer systems that perform tasks such as recognizing, predicting, recommending or generating, and recognize "AI" as a broad umbrella term

AI.BASICS.02.title: Tell software that follows rules a person wrote from a system whose behavior comes from patterns learned from examples

AI.BASICS.03.title: Explain machine learning and deep learning as nested ideas, with deep learning using many-layered neural networks

AI.BASICS.04.title: Classify an AI use as recommending, recognizing, forecasting or generating

AI.BASICS.05.title: Decide whether a task needs new content generated or a label or number predicted, and name a typical failure of each

AI.BASICS.06.title: Tell an AI model from the app or service built around it, and avoid assuming that all AI systems or all chatbots behave the same way

AI.BASICS.07.title: Use human comparisons carefully: say where a comparison helps, where it misleads, and why abilities can be uneven

AI.CHECK.01.title: Recognize a hallucination (confident output that is false or unsupported) and why it happens

AI.CHECK.02.title: Check whether a cited source exists and whether it actually supports the claim attached to it

AI.CHECK.03.title: Recalculate or estimate numbers in an AI response before relying on them

AI.CHECK.04.title: Spot information that may be out of date and check a current, dated source

AI.CHECK.05.title: Tell a claim from evidence for it, and prefer a primary source

AI.CHECK.06.title: Choose an independent check, and explain why asking again or getting two AI tools to agree is not proof

AI.CHECK.07.title: Compare a summary with its source to find omissions, distortions and added claims

AI.CHECK.08.title: Spot contradictions and identify what information is missing before a conclusion can be trusted

AI.CHECK.09.title: Recognize high-stakes questions (health, law, money, safety) where a qualified person must review the answer

AI.CHECK.10.title: Judge usefulness and correctness separately, and explain why results may not repeat exactly

AI.CODE.01.title: Read a few lines of Python with defined terms and predict what they do

AI.CODE.02.title: Explain why code that looks right can still be wrong and how to check it

AI.CODE.03.title: State requirements clearly, including unusual inputs (edge cases)

AI.CODE.04.title: Choose a test whose expected result would reveal a particular defect

AI.CODE.05.title: Use an error message to locate a problem before asking for a fix

AI.CODE.06.title: Use explanations as a starting point and review code line by line against its requirements

AI.CODE.07.title: Explain commits, differences (diffs) and reverting, and why to commit before accepting generated changes

AI.CODE.08.title: Check that a suggested library exists, is the intended one and is trustworthy before installing it

AI.CODE.09.title: Spot exposed secrets and unsafe handling of input in short code examples

AI.CODE.10.title: Keep generated code understandable, documented and owned by someone who can maintain it

AI.COST.01.title: Compare free plans, subscriptions and metered (pay-per-use) pricing for a stated pattern of use

AI.COST.02.title: Estimate a metered cost from token counts and stated input and output rates

AI.COST.03.title: Plan around usage limits and response time (latency)

AI.COST.04.title: Compare running a model through a provider with running one on your own device, including hardware, privacy and upkeep

AI.COST.05.title: Explain that downloadable model weights still come with license terms, and read those terms for a stated use

AI.COST.06.title: Choose a tool from stated needs, limits and costs, including switching costs and avoiding unneeded subscriptions

AI.EVAL.01.title: Build a small test set of real tasks with expected answers before trusting a tool

AI.EVAL.02.title: Read false positives and false negatives from a simple table and say which matters more in a situation

AI.EVAL.03.title: Explain what a benchmark score shows, why it may not match your task, and what contamination means

AI.EVAL.04.title: Weigh accuracy against speed and cost for a stated need

AI.EVAL.05.title: Compare two versions with the same tests and written criteria

AI.EVAL.06.title: Use a rubric for human review and look for failures rather than trusting a demonstration

AI.EVAL.07.title: Choose a measure that matches the goal of a task

AI.EVERYDAY.01.title: Use AI to widen options and draft plans, then choose and check them yourself

AI.EVERYDAY.02.title: Use AI for drafts and edits while keeping your meaning, facts and voice

AI.EVERYDAY.03.title: Request a summary grounded in a supplied text and check it against the source

AI.EVERYDAY.04.title: Use AI translation for understanding, and know when a human translator or check is needed

AI.EVERYDAY.05.title: Use AI in ways that support learning (explanations, practice, feedback) rather than replacing it

AI.EVERYDAY.06.title: Find and follow the AI rules of a class, school or workplace, including disclosure

AI.EVERYDAY.07.title: Use AI for household and travel plans while checking prices, times, rules and safety details

AI.EVERYDAY.08.title: Use AI features such as reading aloud, simplifying, captioning and describing images, and check their accuracy

AI.EVERYDAY.09.title: Choose a calculator, search engine, spreadsheet or official site when it fits the task better than a generative AI tool

AI.EVERYDAY.10.title: Tell requests for facts from requests for invention, and label invented material

AI.FAIR.01.title: Explain how unrepresentative or historical data can lead a model to repeat unfair patterns

AI.FAIR.02.title: Compare error rates across groups in a table and describe a measured disparity accurately

AI.FAIR.03.title: Recognize a proxy (an input that stands in for a protected trait) in a simple example

AI.FAIR.04.title: Explain that different fairness goals can conflict and that choosing one is a decision people must make and explain

AI.FAIR.05.title: Explain why an overall accuracy score can hide poor results for some groups or cases, and plan inclusive testing

AI.FAIR.06.title: Spot stereotypes in generated text or images and plan human review

AI.FAIR.07.title: Evaluate whether an AI feature works for people with different languages, accents and disabilities, using measured evidence

AI.HISTORY.01.title: Place selected early ideas (Turing's 1950 paper, the 1955-56 Dartmouth project) and explain why they matter

AI.HISTORY.02.title: Explain the shift from mainly hand-written rules and search to learning from data, with dated examples

AI.HISTORY.03.title: Describe selected milestones (2012 image recognition, the 2017 transformer, the 2022 chatbot release) and what they changed

AI.HISTORY.04.title: Tell narrow task performance from claims of general intelligence

AI.HISTORY.05.title: Tell recorded events from predictions, and judge the evidence behind a capability claim or headline

AI.HISTORY.06.title: Describe energy and resource demands of AI using dated, sourced estimates and their uncertainty, without one universal per-question number

AI.IMAGE.01.title: Write an image request that states subject, setting, style and composition

AI.IMAGE.02.title: Inspect a generated image for visual errors and unreadable or misspelled text

AI.IMAGE.03.title: Keep characters, colors and details consistent across a series, and request targeted edits

AI.IMAGE.04.title: Check generated diagrams, maps and charts against real data before using them

AI.IMAGE.05.title: Plan a clear presentation and tell a text draft from the separate step of creating and exporting a file

AI.IMAGE.06.title: Make visuals accessible with alt text, readable contrast and clear labels

AI.LAW.01.title: Tell a law, a regulation, a proposed bill, a court ruling, a contract and voluntary guidance apart

AI.LAW.02.title: Apply the US human-authorship requirement to examples, separating what is settled from what is open

AI.LAW.03.title: Describe the open legal questions about training AI on copyrighted works without presenting them as settled

AI.LAW.04.title: Read provider terms and licenses for what they allow and require, and tell a contract from a law

AI.LAW.05.title: Explain likeness and voice rights and consent using dated state and federal examples

AI.LAW.06.title: Recognize privacy rules that can apply to data used with AI, with dated US and EU examples

AI.LAW.07.title: Explain that anti-discrimination and notice rules can apply when AI helps make hiring or credit decisions

AI.LAW.08.title: Recognize deceptive claims about AI products and fake AI-written reviews as consumer-protection issues

AI.LAW.09.title: Follow a written AI policy, disclose AI help where required and keep records

AI.LAW.10.title: Describe the EU AI Act's risk-based approach and dated timeline as an international comparison

AI.LAW.11.title: Identify the facts needed before deciding who is responsible for an AI error

AI.LAW.12.title: Explain why AI rules differ by state and change over time, and check the current, dated status of a rule

AI.LEARN.01.title: Tell training (learning patterns from data) from inference (using the finished model on new input)

AI.LEARN.02.title: Describe parameters as the adjustable numbers a model sets during training, and explain that the model keeps learned patterns, not a copy of every example

AI.LEARN.03.title: Explain why data is split into training, validation and test sets and why test data must stay unseen during training

AI.LEARN.04.title: Recognize overfitting (doing well on familiar examples but poorly on new ones) and what good generalization looks like

AI.LEARN.05.title: Explain how missing, wrong, outdated or unrepresentative data and labels affect what a model learns

AI.LEARN.06.title: Tell supervised, unsupervised and self-supervised learning apart by where the learning signal comes from

AI.LEARN.07.title: Explain reinforcement learning as learning from rewards, and how human ratings are used to adjust language models

AI.LEARN.08.title: Tell fine-tuning (further training that changes a model) from supplying information in a request (which does not change the model)

AI.LLM.01.title: Describe a large language model (LLM) as a model trained on large amounts of text to predict likely next pieces of text, and say what that does and does not imply

AI.LLM.02.title: Explain tokens as the pieces of text a language model reads and writes, and why token counts differ from word counts

AI.LLM.03.title: Explain that a language model chooses among likely next tokens, so the same request can produce different answers

AI.LLM.04.title: Explain why smooth, confident language is not evidence that a statement is correct

AI.LLM.05.title: Explain a context window as the limited amount of text a model can consider at once and predict what happens when a conversation or document exceeds it

AI.LLM.06.title: Tell knowledge learned in training (with a cutoff date) from information supplied or retrieved during a request

AI.LLM.07.title: Tell the text in the current conversation from product features that save information between conversations, and check a product's own settings

AI.LLM.08.title: Explain at a conceptual level how attention lets a model weigh other words in the context, without treating it as a human mind

AI.LLM.09.title: Explain that a product adds its own instructions, settings, tools and limits, so a general description of LLMs cannot predict one product's behavior

AI.MEDIA.01.title: Tell speech-to-text (transcription) from text-to-speech (generation) and check transcripts for errors and speaker labels

AI.MEDIA.02.title: Check generated subtitles and translated audio for timing, meaning and names

AI.MEDIA.03.title: Explain voice cloning and why consent and disclosure matter, using dated legal examples

AI.MEDIA.04.title: Check the rights and terms that apply before using generated music

AI.MEDIA.05.title: Check generated or edited video for consistency over time and disclose synthetic presenters

AI.MEDIA.06.title: Verify surprising images, audio or video by checking the source and context, not one visual oddity

AI.MEDIA.07.title: Explain content credentials and watermarks and why missing labels or detector scores are not proof

AI.PHIL.01.title: Identify the conclusion, premises and assumptions of a short argument about AI

AI.PHIL.02.title: Explain the imitation game and what passing it would and would not show

AI.PHIL.03.title: Explain the Chinese Room argument, a main reply, and what remains disputed

AI.PHIL.04.title: Evaluate what kinds of evidence a claim that an AI is conscious would need, and why fluent self-reports do not settle it

AI.PHIL.05.title: Recognize anthropomorphism (treating a system as if it had human traits) and set trust by evidence

AI.PHIL.06.title: Explain automation bias and keep human judgment and responsibility when using AI help

AI.PHIL.07.title: Explain alignment as getting a system to pursue what people actually intend, including the gap between a stated goal and the intended goal

AI.PHIL.08.title: Compare competing arguments about AI's role by their evidence and values, without treating a disputed view as fact

AI.PITFALL.01.title: Notice overloaded requests and attachments that did not arrive or were not read

AI.PITFALL.02.title: Spot truncated output and formatting errors before using a result

AI.PITFALL.03.title: Check links and dated facts before sharing them

AI.PITFALL.04.title: Keep original files and label draft versions so changes can be compared and undone

AI.PITFALL.05.title: Check files after exporting or moving them between tools, including unsupported file types

AI.PITFALL.06.title: Tell a feature of one interface from a model's ability, and handle account limits, support and cancellation

AI.PRIVACY.01.title: Identify personal and sensitive information in text before sharing it with an AI tool

AI.PRIVACY.02.title: Remove or replace details a task does not need before sharing

AI.PRIVACY.03.title: Decide whether you have permission to share customer, classmate, patient or workplace information with a tool

AI.PRIVACY.04.title: Find and read what a provider says about storing, reviewing and training on your data, and remember practices differ

AI.PROMPT.01.title: Identify the task, context, audience and purpose a request needs, and spot which one is missing

AI.PROMPT.02.title: State the output format and constraints (length, tone, things to avoid) that a result must meet

AI.PROMPT.03.title: Use a short example to show what is wanted, and notice when an example pulls the output away from the written instructions

AI.PROMPT.04.title: Split a large task into stages that can each be checked

AI.PROMPT.05.title: Ask the system to state assumptions or ask questions when the request is missing information

AI.PROMPT.06.title: Write success criteria and use them to revise or compare drafts

AI.PROMPT.07.title: Notice requirements that cannot all be met and resolve the conflict before continuing

AI.PROMPT.08.title: Supply the relevant source material and request structured output, such as a table, that is easy to check

AI.PROMPT.09.title: Explain why role-play, magic phrases, or demands for citations or certainty do not by themselves create expertise or accuracy

AI.RETRIEVAL.01.title: Tell searching (finding existing sources) from generating text, and explain retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) simply

AI.RETRIEVAL.02.title: Check that a source-grounded answer stays within what its sources say

AI.RETRIEVAL.03.title: Tell extracting what a document says from interpreting what it means, and check each

AI.RETRIEVAL.04.title: Recognize when a scan, table or partial document may be read incorrectly or incompletely

AI.RETRIEVAL.05.title: Explain that supplying a document affects that request's context but does not retrain the underlying model

AI.SECURITY.01.title: Keep passwords and access keys out of prompts and code, and avoid sharing accounts

AI.SECURITY.02.title: Recognize scams that use AI-written messages or cloned voices and verify through a trusted channel

AI.SECURITY.03.title: Explain prompt injection and treat instructions inside emails, web pages or documents as untrusted data

AI.WORK.01.title: Analyze how AI may change some tasks in a job without assuming the whole occupation disappears or stays the same

AI.WORK.02.title: Read an employment forecast as a projection with assumptions and uncertainty

AI.WORK.03.title: Describe what data scientists, machine learning engineers and AI engineers typically do, without inventing pay or credential rules

AI.WORK.04.title: Describe AI-related roles that rely on evaluation, data work, product, design, governance and subject knowledge

AI.WORK.05.title: Plan a learning route and portfolio evidence that matches a stated goal, with no guaranteed outcome

AI.WORK.06.title: Spot exaggerated AI income, job or course promises and check them

AI.WORK.07.title: Follow approved tools, protect confidential information and review AI output before it reaches others at work
